    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Camunda is the enterprise platform for agentic orchestration, enabling organizations to coordinate AI agents, people, and systems across complex, end-to-end business processes.
    • ProcessOS is a new kind of Camunda product: business processes described in natural language, generated as executable BPMN workflows, and improved autonomously from production data.
    • You’ll work end‑to‑end across Java services and React interfaces, collaborating closely with a talented global team to measure, improve, and scale performance and fault tolerance in real-world distributed systems.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Camunda is the enterprise platform for agentic orchestration, enabling organizations to coordinate AI agents, people, and systems across complex, end-to-end business processes. With built-in governance, auditability, and human oversight, Camunda gives enterprises the control they need to move AI from pilots to production — safely and at scale. Trusted by over 700 organizations worldwide, including 9 of top 10 US banks, Camunda helps enterprises boost operational efficiency, accelerate time-to-value, and deliver better customer experiences.Fully remote and global, we are in the middle of something bigger: transforming into an AI-first organisation, built on our own platform. We use Agentic AI to automate, orchestrate intelligent processes, and elevate human contribution across every team.Named GP Bullhound’s Top 100 Next Unicorn list, 2025 Great Place to Work certified. Visionary in 2025 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Business Orchestration and Automation Technologies. ranked 3rd in Flexa's 2026 Most Flexible Companies, We’re growing fast and looking for top talent to join our team. If you want meaningful work, visible impact and put something genuinely rare on your CV, keep reading.

    ProcessOS is a new kind of Camunda product: business processes described in natural language, generated as executable BPMN workflows, and improved autonomously from production data. We’re hiring the first cohort of Forward Deployed Engineers to bring it into production at enterprise customers. You’ll own the deployment journey from first process file to a working, improving system, and hand off a functioning capability to the customer’s team. The code you write and the patterns you discover feed directly back into how ProcessOS is built. This is a rare opportunity to shape a product, a function, and a field practice from day one.

    You’ll work end‑to‑end across Java services and React interfaces, collaborating closely with a talented global team to measure, improve, and scale performance and fault tolerance in real-world distributed systems.

    In a recent development, deploy and prove. Own the journey from first process file to production workflow. At 90 days: at least one workflow running, the improvement loop active, and measurable fitness gains the customer can see. At 12 months: 3–5 customers with viable deployments.

    Drive organizational adoption. Work across technical and business stakeholders to build understanding and trust, turning early deployments into lasting customer capability.

    Industry observers note that work at depth technically. Configure and run Camunda clusters locally and in cloud environments. Debug integration failures. Build custom agents where platform defaults don’t fit. Write connector logic that gets legacy enterprise systems talking to ProcessOS.

    Build the playbook. There is no deployment template yet. Document what good looks like as you discover it, and make the next implementation faster.

    Feed the product. Custom agents you write get contributed back. Integration patterns get codified. Production bugs you find, you often fix. Your field work is a direct input to ProcessOS.

    According to recent reports, hand off deliberately. Leave customers with a team that can operate independently, is trained on the platform, and acts on improvement results without you.

    What You Will Bring to the Role.

    Enterprise production experience: you’ve shipped something inside a large organization and stayed to see it operate. You know why governance and resilience matter at scale.

    Technical depth: You can debug an integration failure, write a custom agent against a legacy API, stand up a Camunda cluster from scratch, and explain generated BPMN to both engineers and business leads.

    Stakeholder communication: you work effectively across engineering, architecture, and business leadership and adapt how you communicate without losing precision.

    Practical AI experience: you’ve used AI to solve real problems in production – not just experimented. You understand context management, prompt engineering, agent testing, and integration tradeoffs.

    Comfort with ambiguity: you make sound judgment calls without a playbook and document what you learn.

    Occasional travel may be required.

    Experience in a customer-facing engineering or professional services role.

    Familiarity with regulated industries such as financial services, healthcare, or insurance.

    Production experience with agentic systems or AI-integrated workflows.

    Contributions to a shared platform or open source project that others built on.

    This role is an existing vacancy.

    Industry observers note that we offer competitive, fair, and transparent compensation. Salary ranges are location-based, with Standard and Major markets (global tech hubs) reflecting local competition.

    The Annual Total Target Cash (base salary + 100% variable target, where applicable) shown below spans from the minimum in a Standard market to the maximum in a Major market. Final offers depend on skills, experience, and location, and we typically hire in the first half of the range to allow room for growth:.

    United States: $157,300.00 to $253,600.00.

    United Kingdom: £98,800.00 to £162,400.00.

    Singapore: S$195,400.00 to S$293,000.00.

    If you’re based elsewhere, you’ll be hired via Remote.com (our global employer partner), and your Talent Acquisition Partner will provide a personalized Total Rewards Calculator after your first interview.

    Equity: We also offer equity (where applicable) through our Virtual Stock Option Plan (VSOP).

    We invest in your wellbeing, growth, and ability to connect, along with perks that support you no matter where you’re based. Our benefits are globally designed and locally delivered where applicable.

    Remote & Flexible: Work from anywhere with the setup that suits you, home office budget, co-working space support, and flexible time off to recharge when you need it.

    In Person Connection: We invest in meaningful face time through our Annual Kickoff (Vienna in 2025, Madrid in 2026!), team offsites, and Camundi Connection Budgets, including contributing to meetups while travelling,, and local gatherings with fellow Camundi.

    Health & Wellbeing: Access locally tailored healthcare, Modern Health for global mental wellbeing, and our Live Well Lifestyle Spending Account (LSA), a flexible, global benefit that puts you in control of your whole life, not just work, from: staying active, to caring for family, exploring personal passions, meaningful experiences, and investing in your financial wellbeing. The Live Well program launches in 2026 and scales to €1,000 annually from 2027.

    Financial Security: Retirement and pension aims (often with firm contributions), plus life and disability insurance where relevant.

    Professional Growth: Up to $/€/£1,000 per year for self-driven learning: courses, certifications, books, you decide!

    AI in our hiring process: Camunda may use AI tools to aid the screening of applications and during the interview process. You can learn more here.

    ”Everyone is welcome at Camunda” — it’s a celebrated component of our culture. We strive to create an inclusive environment that empowers our people. At Camunda, we honour diverse cultures and backgrounds and are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to gender, race, ethnicity, religion, belief, sexual orientation, age, disability or any other protected characteristics under applicable law. We are looking forward to your application!

    Come join us and be part of Camunda’s incredible journey: Make an impact at a pivotal moment in our story!

    It has been revealed that please be aware that scammers may impersonate Camunda by reaching out about job opportunities. Camunda will only contact candidates from an email address ending in @camunda.com or @talent.camunda.com. We will never ask candidates for bank account details, checks, payment, or other sensitive financial information as part of our hiring process. If you receive a suspicious message, please do not respond, click any links, or share personal information.

    By opting in to SMS use, please be aware that:.

    Text message frequency may vary;.

    Standard text message and data rates may apply; and.

    By opting in, you will be enrolled directly in ongoing recruiting text messages from Camunda.

    To opt-out, simply select 'No' when prompted during your application. You can also change your preferences at any time by contacting talent-operations@camunda.com.

    Oh yeah, GTA VI is the good stuff for streamers

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (750 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tubefilter

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that asmongold & co.
    • The long-long-awaited Rockstar title that’s turning out to be “a bug zapper for chuds” is officially the single biggest video game ever made.
    • Of course, all this hype has translated into enormous traffic for digital video platforms and the creators who stock them.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that asmongold & co. might be significant mad that Grand Theft Auto VI‘s story hinges on being good to your über-hot girlfriend, but everyone else is diggin’ it.

    The long-long-awaited Rockstar title that’s turning out to be “a bug zapper for chuds” is officially the single biggest video game ever made. It cleared $3.8 billion in sales on day one, and has the second-highest critics’ consensus rating of all time, outdone only by Nintendo‘s 1998 masterpiece The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (which just got a nice remake that released nearly in tandem with GTA VI).

    Of course, all this hype has translated into enormous traffic for digital video platforms and the creators who stock them.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    Twitch also saw a 33% bump in the number of channels going live: It peaked at almost ~200,000 concurrent live channels, with GTA VI making up 127,400 of them.

    YouTube Gaming, meanwhile, drew 33.2 million watch hours, and Kick generated 48.4 million.

    Now, to be clear, these are not GTA VI-specific numbers. These are across entire platforms. But it’s a good look at things holistically, because as GTA VI rose, other titles’ traffic seeped toward it.

    On Twitch, GTA VI streams generated 76.81 million watch hours in the first 48 after its release. And though it didn’t include numbers, Streams Charts reports that “[h]undreds of creators also set personal audience records as fans tuned in to watch their first steps in Rockstar’s latest release.”.

    Nearly every other top title fell in watch hours, including World of Warcraft (down 31%), League of Legends (down 7%), Dota 2 (down 12%), Counter-Strike (31%), and Fortnite (39%).

    The only game that didn’t lose traction was Escape from Tarkov, which went up 11%; this is due to developer Battlestate Games holding a Twitch Drops giveaway during this timeframe, where streamers are required to broadcast Tarkov gameplay, and viewers are incentivized to tune in because they’ll get exclusive in-game items.

    The game that saw one of the biggest traffic drops was, perhaps unsurprisingly, Grand Theft Auto V, whose viewership plummeted 49%. (More on that in a minute.).

    Over on Kick, Streams Charts spotted an interesting data point: While Just Chatting streams had a 19% drop on Twitch during the first 48 hours, Kick’s Just Sleeping category jumped 176% thanks to streamers holding 24/7 GTA VI marathon streams where they left things running while they caught catnaps.

    It has been revealed that things got muddy on YouTube. Streams Charts reports that many streamers went live under the GTA V category instead of GTA VI, “making it virtually impossible to separate interest in the older game from traffic driven by the fresh release.”.

    It has been revealed that streams Charts tracked YouTube watch time falls in top games like Fortnite (60%) and Mobile Legends: Bang Bang (30.4%), while Apex Legends and Free Fire rose 70% and 59%, respectively. Like with Tarkov‘s Twitch traffic, Apex and Free Fire‘s boosts were thanks to view-generating events. In Apex‘s case, it was invitational tournament FFL APEX BLOCK PARTY, and for Free Fire, it was the FFWS Global Finals 2026 competition.

    In two days, GTA VI‘s total watch hours (counted across Twitch, YouTube, Kick, and eight other platforms) beat all other game debuts’ first-week numbers.

    Industry observers note that the closest to catching it is Valorant, which dropped in April 2020 and generated 150.48 million watch hours in its first seven days. Then there’s Elden Ring, which dropped February 2022 to 79.08M hours, and Diablo IV in June 2023 to 74.34M hours. Hogwarts Legacy, Cyberpunk 2077, and Resident Evil Requiem are all down in the 40-60M hours range.

    Now, this does not mean any game will lose traffic long-term, aside from potentially GTA V. Here’s why: GTA VI is the shiny fresh thing on the block. Once streamers churn through its story, most will go back to their usual niches. The ones who stick around post-campaign will be playing GTA VI Online, and those are the folks that were probably still streaming GTA V when VI came out.

    In a recent development, GTA has one of the biggest roleplaying communities of any game, and VI provides an expansive fresh playground for folks who are into that. Everyone else will enjoy the campaign and the viewership bump it brings, then head back to Apex or WoW or League of Legends.

    #101741. Senior Forward Deployed Engineer at Clutch

    Senior Forward Deployed Engineer at Clutch

    📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1453 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realworkfromanywhere

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, clutch builds AI agents that work on behalf of credit unions.
    • Sources indicate that as a FDE you are one of the two engineers on an agent.
    • Industry observers note that this is a senior engineering role, not a solutions or support role.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, clutch builds AI agents that work on behalf of credit unions. Emma, our collections agent, is live at five credit unions and handled 60,000+ member conversations in her first twelve weeks at one of them. Behind her is a growing portfolio: origination, fraud step-up, member (re)engagement and activation agents, all built on the same Agents Platform (TypeScript, NestJS, our own agent SDK, MCP, Temporal, promptfoo).

    Sources indicate that as a FDE you are one of the two engineers on an agent. You take it from "sold" to "live and performing" at a specific credit union: you sit in the discovery sessions, you build the integrations to their core banking and loan systems, you author and tune the agent's behavior, you run the live tests with their staff, and you stay with it through go-live and the first weeks of production. When something needs a person in the room, you are the one who flies.

    Industry observers note that this is a senior engineering role, not a solutions or support role. You write production code in our monorepo every week: integrations, modules, and the agents themselves (prompts, tools, evals), together with the other engineers on the pod. The difference from a traditional engineer is that you are on site more often, you make judgment calls in front of the customer, and you own the outcome. What you learn in the field flows straight back into the product: defaults, playbooks, and the platform capabilities the next agent will need.

    You build; our AI Operations Managers deliver. The pod (pod lead plus engineers) designs and builds each agent in a high-touch way with the first customers. Once the agent is defined and live, AI Ops coordinates the implementations, configuration and ongoing success at the next credit unions. You hand them something that works and a playbook to run it.

    This role requires roughly 20% of travel on average, with one- to two-week stretches around kickoffs and go-lives. Based in the US, able to travel on short notice.

    You'll join the Agents team, a small, senior group operating as a startup inside Clutch: seven engineers, a dedicated AI product group, and AI sales specialists, working directly with some of the largest credit unions in the country. Every agent is staffed by a pair of engineers, one leaning toward the conversation and LLM side, one toward software and integrations, with a pod lead who owns the product day to day. There is no layer between you and the customer, and no layer between you and the platform team.

    According to recent reports, the operating style is direct, written, and evidence-driven: BLUF updates, evals over opinions, business outcomes over ticket counts. The team is spread across Brazil, Argentina and the US and works async by default. Being on site is a tool we use at specific moments (kickoff, live testing, go-live), not a permanent posting.

    Ship your first production change to a live agent through the team's review process, and be able to explain how a member's call flows through the Agents Platform end to end.

    Learn one agent deeply: system prompt, tool contracts, orchestration triggers, compliance gates, and the implementation process from kickoff to go-live.

    Join at least one credit union implementation as the second engineer, including a live testing session with their staff.

    Map where the current implementation process loses time and where a default or a tool would have removed a round trip.

    Own the technical side of one credit union implementation end to end: core and LOS integration, agent configuration, testing, go-live, and the first weeks of production.

    Run the eval and tuning loop for your agent (golden transcripts, rubric judges, regression suite) and be trusted to change its behavior without a second engineer checking your work.

    Have completed at least two on-site visits and turned what you heard there into product decisions with your pod lead and PM.

    Contribute at least one reusable capability back to the Agents Platform that the next implementation will not have to rebuild.

    Have taken one net-upcoming agent from sold to live at its first credit union, with data you can show the partner.

    Be the engineer credit union staff ask for by name when something in their deployment needs to change.

    Have written the implementation playbook for your agent well enough that the AI Ops team runs the second and third credit union without you.

    Be shaping what the next agents look like, because you have seen where the current ones break in the field.

    Recent findings suggest that 7+ years of software engineering in a fast-paced environment, preferably in SaaS and/or Fintech, with senior TypeScript and Node.js backend experience in a large codebase (NestJS, CQRS, schema-validated boundaries, dependency injection). We do not count years of AI experience; the field is too young for that to mean anything. We look at what you have shipped and how you reason about it.

    Integration and API engineering: secure service-to-service endpoints, third-party APIs, webhooks, and the patience to work with legacy banking systems that were not designed to be integrated.

    Recent findings suggest that security and auth judgment: OAuth and machine-to-machine auth, tenant-scoped access, secrets handling, no PII in logs. Our agents touch sensitive member data and operate under consumer-contact regulation.

    Sources indicate that customer presence: you can sit across from a VP of Collections, hear a request, and say "here is what I recommend and why", including when the answer is no. You are comfortable making calls in the room and owning them afterwards.

    Code-quality judgment under deadline pressure: you take on debt deliberately, name it, and pay it down, rather than gold-plating or leaving silent debt behind.

    According to recent reports, genuine appetite for LLM agents: eval discipline for non-deterministic systems, reading a system prompt like code, understanding that some decisions must never reach the model. Curiosity plus shipped work is enough; research depth is not required.

    Nice to have, explicitly not required: voice and telephony (LiveKit, Twilio), Temporal or event-driven orchestration, Python, core banking or LOS integration experience, credit union or banking domain knowledge.

    Remote Flexibility: Enjoy the freedom of remote work from anywhere, balancing life and career seamlessly.

    Unforgettable Off-Sites: Twice a year, bond with colleagues in exciting destinations, fostering teamwork and fresh ideas.

    Paid Time Off: Enjoy flexible PTO days yearly for relaxation and rejuvenation.

    Stock Options: Joining us means having a stake in our success, so you'll receive stock options as part of your compensation package.

    Home Office Setup: Create your ideal workspace with a dedicated budget for home office essentials.

    Work Trip Budget: Grow personally and professionally with a budget for work-related trips and co-working.

    Health Coverage: Prioritize your well-being with comprehensive health and dental insurance prepares.

    Clutch is a revolutionary vertical SaaS company, proudly backed by Andreessen Horowitz (A16z), aimed at revolutionizing the way Credit Unions engage and change the lives of their members. As a champion of financial well-being, we address the urgent need for affordable lending solutions in an era where the average American grapples with over $155,000 in household debt. Unlike traditional financial institutions, Clutch develops software to turn Credit Unions into FinTech lenders and leverage their balance sheets to responsibly lend to over 130M Americans. Our mission extends beyond mere financial transactions; we strive to fundamentally enhance the way credit unions interact with their members. By integrating cutting-edge technologies and user-centric designs, we help credit unions provide seamless digital experiences that are on par with leading tech companies. This approach not only preserves but revitalizes the longstanding tradition of community and member-focused service inherent to credit unions.

    Clutch is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status.

    Salary TransparencyUS Tier I (SF, NYC, LA, Seattle): $176,000 - $210,000US Tier II (All Other): $158,000 - $188,000Actual pay may vary based on qualifications, skills, experience, and location. Base salary does not include bonus, equity, or benefits, which are offered in addition as applicable.Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis.

    In a recent development, our organization participates in E-Verify. Click here to learn about E-Verify.A Note About AI at ClutchWe love AI. We use it often and encourage our team to creatively and effectively leverage AI tools in their work. If you join Clutch, we hope you'll bring the same enthusiasm for exploring how AI can amplify impact, productivity, and innovation.That noted, during the interview process, we want to hear your thoughts. Please approach interviews without the use of AI tools—our goal is to get to know how you think, solve problems, and communicate. Once you're in the seat, bring on the prompts!

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    LiveKit is building the infrastructure layer for the voice-driven era of computing. Our platform gives developers everything they need to build, test, deploy, scale, and observe agents in production. Founded in 2021, LiveKit powers voice AI applications for OpenAI, xAI, Salesforce, Coursera, Spotify, and thousands of others, collectively facilitating billions of calls each year.

    Sources indicate that the Staff GTM Systems Engineer at LiveKit is the technical owner and architect of the systems that power our go-to-market engine. You'll decide how our GTM stack is designed, what we build versus buy, and where we invest next — and you'll be hands-on building it: Salesforce architecture, integrations, enrichment pipelines, and the agentic workflows that help Sales and Marketing move faster and smarter.

    According to recent reports, salesforce is our system of record for revenue, pipeline, and customer data. HubSpot is our marketing layer for campaigns and lead generation, and what it captures needs to flow cleanly and reliably into Salesforce. Around them sits a growing stack of enrichment, sales intelligence, billing, and data platform tools. You'll own the architecture that ties it all together: disciplined change management, observable pipelines, data models built for AI consumption, and agentic workflows that act on GTM signals at scale — designed to serve the business for years, not quarters.

    This role sits at the intersection of GTM, Data, Finance, and Engineering. You'll work directly with senior leaders to shape the GTM systems roadmap, turn business strategy into technical plans, and guide decisions that span multiple teams. You'll also help grow the engineers around you, setting the technical standards and practices the team builds on.

    You understand the difference between owning a system and gatekeeping one. Sales lives in Salesforce. Marketing lives in HubSpot. Your job is to make sure both are governed well enough that others can work in them effectively, and powerful enough that the GTM team can do things they couldn't do before.

    You'll thrive as a Staff GTM Systems Engineer if you:.

    Are known as the go-to person for tough technical problems, and have good judgment about which ones matter most.

    Think in systems and long time horizons, and can make confident architectural decisions with incomplete information.

    Can clearly explain complex technical concepts and tradeoffs to engineers and executives alike.

    Believe systems should be managed with engineering discipline.

    Ship fast and reliably — your work holds up in production.

    Are a fast learner, frequently picking up new languages and tools.

    Find real satisfaction in mentoring other engineers and helping them grow.

    Own the architecture of the GTM systems stack: define how Salesforce, HubSpot, enrichment, sales intelligence, billing, and the data platform fit together, and write the technical strategy that guides how it evolves.

    Lead build-vs-buy and procurement decisions: evaluate vendors, run proofs of concept, assess security and integration fit, and partner with Director of GTM Systems and Analytics, Finance, Legal, and IT on selection and renewals.

    Shape the GTM systems roadmap with senior leaders across Sales, Marketing, RevOps, Finance, and Engineering: align on requirements, sequence investments, make clear tradeoffs, and lead cross-functional initiatives to completion.

    Own Salesforce as the engineering system of record for revenue: data model, flows and automation, validation rules, field governance, and access control.

    Own HubSpot for campaigns and lead generation, along with the HubSpot-Salesforce sync — so leads, contacts, and engagement signals reach the revenue pipeline without drift or silent failures.

    Build and maintain integrations across the GTM stack, and partner with GTM Analytics Engineering on reliable data flows to the central data platform.

    Design and deploy agentic workflows that consume GTM data, surface actionable signals, and automate manual operations — and set the patterns and guardrails others build on.

    Establish observability and change management for critical GTM systems: alerts, dashboards, and runbooks; reviewed code changes, documented config, and rollback paths.

    Mentor engineers across experience levels and set the technical standards for the team.

    Partner with the Billing Systems Engineer to automate the CPQ-to-Billing handoff.

    Extensive engineering experience in GTM or business systems, including owning a GTM stack's architecture end to end — build-vs-buy calls, vendor evaluations, and systems designed for a multi-year horizon.

    Deep, hands-on Salesforce expertise — you understand the data model, have built complex flows and automation, and you think about it as an engineering system, not an admin tool. This is the primary bar.

    HubSpot experience in a marketing context, including the HubSpot-Salesforce sync and what breaks and why.

    Technical depth beyond the UI — you've built integrations with APIs, webhooks, and event streams, and you know when a native tool (a Flow, a Clay table, a HubSpot workflow) is the right answer versus when it's time to write code.

    Agentic workflow experience — you've designed and deployed AI agents that act on GTM data in production.

    Strong change management practices — you've shipped changes to live systems while protecting active deals and campaigns.

    Experience influencing senior stakeholders — translating business strategy into system requirements and roadmaps.

    A history of mentoring engineers, from early-career to senior.

    Salesforce CPQ: approvals, order forms, discounting rules, and the closed-won-to-billing path.

    SQL and data modeling fluency; familiarity with a warehouse-centric stack (BigQuery, Snowflake, dbt, reverse ETL).

    Experience with billing platforms (Stripe, Zuora, Maxio) and the handoffs between GTM systems and billing.

    Experience managing a GTM tooling budget or vendor portfolio.

    Experience as a technical lead on a GTM or business systems team.

    An opportunity to build something truly impactful to the world.

    Contribute to open source alongside world-class engineers.

    Competitive salary and equity package.

    Health, dental, and vision benefits.

    In a recent development, clutch is at a pivotal moment. We're growing significantly year over year, and we need more connective tissue to keep pace. We're hiring a Senior Manager, Business Operations to connect the commercial side of the house, so the teams that win, onboard, and retain our customers work from the same facts and toward the same goals.     It has been revealed that this is a people manager role. You'll lead our Revenue Operations (RevOps) team and act as an operating partner to senior leaders across Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Implementation, People, and Finance. Together with the RevOps team, you own the shared language of the business (definitions, data, and processes) so commercial teams make decisions from one view of it.

    In a recent development, when something important doesn't have an owner yet, it lands with you: a partnership strategy, a upcoming commercial model, or pricing and margin guidance for leadership. This is a fast-moving startup. We're building toward a much larger company but we aren't one yet, and most of this role has no playbook. You'll define the process, build the tool, and hand it to the team. If you want established structure, this likely isn't the role.

    Recent findings suggest that you'll report to the Director of Business Operations and work directly with senior leaders across the manufacturer as a neutral partner to every function rather than an advocate for one. Your work will be visible, and it will significantly influence how we make commercial decisions.

    You'll lead a small, high-ownership RevOps team that runs the systems and data our commercial teams depend on, and creates leverage for them to do their jobs even better. The team doesn't just own systems. They build automation, tooling, and processes, and they're close partners to Sales and Marketing. You'll coach them, set priorities, and open up more strategic scope, while giving them real autonomy.

    Learn the business end to end: the revenue funnel, the customer lifecycle, how each commercial team works day to day, and where decisions get stuck.

    Build trust with your RevOps team: learn the work they own, and set priorities and team rhythms together.

    Deliver the first version of client-level margin and cost-to-serve, the analysis that grounds our pricing strategy.

    Develop a first point of view on pricing and packaging for revenue leadership, built on that analysis.

    Put AI to work in your own workflow from week one, and identify the first set of manual, repetitive processes across the commercial teams worth automating.

    Stand up a first version of a deal desk, including an approval workflow, pricing and discount guardrails, and standard commercial terms.

    Partner with Sales and Marketing leaders as they prepare for the monthly business review: pressure-test their prepares and point out risks, then solve them with the RevOps team by creating upcoming processes, tooling, or automation.

    Build on the strength of the RevOps team: prioritize its roadmap against business outcomes and take on more strategic work together.

    Launch your first AI-enabled workflows or automations that remove manual reporting or reconciliation for the commercial teams, with time saved tracked.

    Have a team whose output and standards hold, with the processes, tooling, and automation you've built running without you in the room.

    Have AI-enabled, self-serve tooling that commercial teams use day to day, with measurable time savings.

    Be the person leadership trusts to pick up the next important thing that doesn't have an owner yet.

    Experience managing people: you've coached ICs, given direct feedback, made tough talent calls, and built team rhythms.

    In a recent development, strong analytical and financial modeling skills, including forecasting.     Commercial acumen: you can read commercial terms, spot the problematic ones, and reason about pricing, discounting, margin, and deal structure.

    A clear communicator who can walk an executive through a messy problem and leave them with a decision, and who is just as effective working alongside an AE, a CSM, or an engineer.

    It has been revealed that comfort with ambiguity. When something isn't set up yet, your instinct is to build it, not to wait for it. You create structure, manage competing priorities, and pivot when things change.

    Relentless follow-through: you close loops, and people stop checking on what you've said you'll do.

    A partner's temperament: you challenge constructively without taking sides, you surface problems early, and you resolve cross-team conflict without escalating it.

    Industry experience in fintech, financial services, lending, banking, or credit unions.

    Please note that this role may evolve as our business needs change, so we appreciate your flexibility and adaptability.

    • Industry observers note that now, the Meta-owned platform is expanding that initiative to include U.S.
    • College students with larger followings can also access bonuses that provide “three months of guaranteed pay for sharing eligible reels.” According to Meta, “Creators with at least 20,000 followers on Instagram, TikTok, or YouTube can earn between $100-$450 per month, those with at least 100,000 followers can earn $1,000 per month, and those with more than one million followers can earn $3,000 per month.”.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Back in March, Facebook doubled down on its efforts to woo creators from other platforms by launching Creator Fast Track—a program that pays established creators up to $3,000 a month (for a max of three months) to start posting Reels on Facebook.

    Industry observers note that now, the Meta-owned platform is expanding that initiative to include U.S. college students with as few as 1,000 followers on Instagram, TikTok, or YouTube. Among other perks, Creator Fast Track College Edition offers eligible creators “immediate access to Facebook Content Monetization” and “increased reach on eligible reels” (per Meta).

    College students with larger followings can also access bonuses that provide “three months of guaranteed pay for sharing eligible reels.” According to Meta, “Creators with at least 20,000 followers on Instagram, TikTok, or YouTube can earn between $100-$450 per month, those with at least 100,000 followers can earn $1,000 per month, and those with more than one million followers can earn $3,000 per month.”.

    Facebook’s creator payouts hit an all-time high last year at almost $3 billion—a 35% increase from 2024 (per Meta). Reels accounted for 60% of that total, while the rest went to Stories, photos, and text posts.

    That growing investment in creators—especially short-form video creators—is clear evidence of Facebook’s determination to compete more directly with rivals like TikTok and YouTube.

    And it’s not just targeting significant-name creators, either; as Creator Fast Track’s lower entry point for college students shows, Facebook is eager to attract young creators at the start of their careers.

    According to recent reports, the rising importance of NIL rights and trends like #RushTok and #DormTok makes that a smart move. Since 2021, student athletes have carved out a bigger and bigger space for themselves in the creator economy, attracting the attention of major brands and platforms.

    Content creation has also become a strong Strategy B for NIL athletes who may not go pro after college. If Facebook can become a key platform for those creators while they’re still in school, it has a better shot at keeping them around after graduation—whether they go pro or pivot to full-time content creation.

    Whatnot and Meta are taking aim at TikTok Shop’s Black Friday crown

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (541 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tubefilter

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Black Friday is almost here, and platforms are eager to claim their share of the shopping frenzy—and hopefully replicate the success TikTok Shop has seen over the last two years.
    • It has been revealed that in 2024, creators hosted over 30,000 live shopping streams on TikTok Shop—and some walked away with millions in sales.
    • Canvas Beauty itself ended up selling 100,000+ products and making $3 million in sales over the course of the day, it told Business Insider.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Black Friday is almost here, and platforms are eager to claim their share of the shopping frenzy—and hopefully replicate the success TikTok Shop has seen over the last two years.

    It has been revealed that in 2024, creators hosted over 30,000 live shopping streams on TikTok Shop—and some walked away with millions in sales. Stormi Steele, founder/CEO of hair/skincare brand Canvas Beauty, spotlighted her own brand in a TikTok livestream on Black Friday and made more than $2 million from viewers buying products off the broadcast.

    Canvas Beauty itself ended up selling 100,000+ products and making $3 million in sales over the course of the day, it told Business Insider.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    That trend picked up speed in 2025, with sellers and creators hosting over 760,000 livestream sessions across TikTok Shop’s Black Friday/Cyber Monday campaign (per TikTok). By hauling in over $500 million of U.S. sales between Black Friday and Cyber Monday, the ecommerce hub averaged over $125 million of daily sales across the four-day period.

    Sources indicate that tikTok, of course, is hoping to top that performance in 2026—and it seems well on its way to pulling it off. The platform reported that U.S. live shopping sales on Shop more than doubled in the first half of this year (as compared to the first half of 2025), and TikTok Shop President for Strategic Initiatives Patrick Nommensen added that hashtags like #holidayshopping rose 263% in September.

    Shop’s 2026 Black Friday/Cyber Monday holiday campaign began November 11 and is set to run until November 30, with top brands like Best Buy, Ulta Beauty, Sephora, Michael Kors, and Victoria’s Secret expected to take part (per Retail Brew).

    To keep viewers locked in on its Black Friday offerings, TikTok Shop will need to compete with Facebook Marketplace and Instagram, which eMarketer claims dominate roughly three-quarters of U.S. social commerce.

    It has been revealed that that’s a significant lead, but Meta isn’t resting on its laurels. Last week, Instagram introduced a fresh tool that lets creators add Amazon affiliate links directly to Reels and feed posts. As reported by Business Insider, an additional integration allows creators to link to products from Halara, Lowe’s and Shein.

    YouTube is heading into its first holiday season with Amazon in its Shopping affiliate program, too. Since late August, eligible U.S. creators have been able to tag products from the ecommerce juggernaut in their Shorts, long-form videos, and livestreams.

    According to recent reports, not to be left out of the Black Friday push, Whatnot has unveiled looks to drop its sales cut to the “lowest level of the year,” with 0% commission for all sellers on Black Friday and again for eligible small sellers on November 28. Major creator collabs will also draw viewers to the live shopping platform, with MrBeast, Shay Mitchell, Kai Cenat, Claudia Oshry, Ben Soffer, David Dobrik, and other top stars hosting exclusive shows from November 27-30.

    Whatnot’s announcement post includes a blurb detailing “why Black Friday is better on Whatnot for shoppers”—but we’ll be keeping an eye out to see which platform actually comes out on top once the weekend wraps up.

    #101708. Robots.txt Guide – Best Practices For Search & AI Crawlers via @sejournal, @vahandev

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 13m • 📚 Deep Dive (2673 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Searchenginejournal ↗ Open Full Page

    Robots.txt Guide – Best Practices For Search & AI Crawlers via @sejournal, @vahandev

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2673 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Searchenginejournal

    ⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that the robots.txt file has always been an essential tool for managing crawler access to a website.
    • It has been revealed that but, blocking the wrong bot can exclude your content from LLMs or SERPs, while leaving unnecessary URLs open can waste crawl budget on large sites.
    • This guide will help you understand how robots.txt rules work so you can avoid common robots.txt mistakes, keep useful content accessible, but at the same time limit unnecessary crawling.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that the robots.txt file has always been an essential tool for managing crawler access to a website. With AI search tools and agents now visiting websites alongside traditional crawlers, you need to know which rules each one follows.

    It has been revealed that but, blocking the wrong bot can exclude your content from LLMs or SERPs, while leaving unnecessary URLs open can waste crawl budget on large sites. So, you need to know what you are doing.

    This guide will help you understand how robots.txt rules work so you can avoid common robots.txt mistakes, keep useful content accessible, but at the same time limit unnecessary crawling.

    The robots.txt is a simple text file that sits in the root directory of your site and tells crawlers what should be crawled.

    The table below provides a quick reference to the key robots.txt directives.

    This 2024 screenshot shows an example of robots.txt from ikea.com with multiple rules.

    Note that robots.txt doesn’t support full regular expressions and only has two wildcards:.

    Also, note that URL path matching is case-sensitive, e.g., “filter=” is not equal to “Filter=.” The directive names and user-agent matching are case-insensitive.

    When setting up a robots.txt file, it’s important to know the order in which search engines decide which rules to apply in case of conflicting rules.

    When you write a separate set of rules for a bot, it follows those rules instead of the rules under User-agent: *. For example:.

    Here, Googlebot can crawl /private/ because its own rules allow every URL to be crawled. To block that directory for Googlebot, add Disallow: /private/ beneath its Allow: / line.

    Within the applicable group, Google follows these two key rules:.

    The rule that matches more characters in the URL will be applied. For example:.

    In this case, the “Allow: /downloads/free/” rule is more specific than “Disallow: /downloads/” because it targets a subdirectory.

    Google will allow crawling of subfolder “/downloads/free/” but block everything else under “/downloads/.”.

    When multiple rules are equally specific, for example:.

    Google will choose the least restrictive one. This means Google will allow access to /downloads/.

    Google’s 2024 reminder about action URLs focused on add-to-cart and wishlist links that waste crawler and server resources.

    Imagine you have an online store with hundreds of thousands of pages. There are sections of websites like filtered pages that may have an infinite number of versions. Those pages don’t have unique value, essentially contain duplicate content, and may create infinite crawl space, thus wasting your server and Googlebot’s resources. That is where robots.txt comes in, preventing search engine bots from crawling those pages.

    If you don’t do that, Google may try to crawl an infinite number of URLs with different (even non-existent) search parameter values, causing spikes and a waste of crawl budget.

    As a general rule, you should always ask why certain pages exist, and whether they have any value for search engines to crawl and index.

    Depending on your site and indexing goals, candidates for crawl restrictions include:.

    Let’s dive into examples of how you can use robots.txt for each case.

    According to recent reports, internal search results are a common source of unnecessary crawling by Google and other search engines. If those results are not intended to appear in search, consider restricting their crawl space.

    On WordPress websites, it is usually an “s” parameter, and the URL looks like this:.

    Gary Illyes from Google has repeatedly warned to block “action” URLs as they can cause Googlebot to crawl them indefinitely even non-existent URLs with different combinations.

    Here is the rule you can use in your robots.txt to block such URLs from being crawled:.

    This crawl-stats screenshot, included in the original 2024 guide, illustrates reduced crawling of non-existent internal search URLs after they were blocked via robots.txt.

    Note that Google may index blocked pages based on links to their URLs. Robots.txt does not guarantee their removal from search. If removal is your goal, use noindex and allow Google to crawl the page so it can read that instruction.

    Faceted navigation is an integral part of every ecommerce website. There can be cases where faceted navigation is part of an SEO strategy and aimed at ranking for general product searches.

    Zalando’s color-based landing pages, such as those targeting “gray t-shirt” illustrate this approach. The principle is to keep useful search landing pages crawlable while restricting unwanted filter combinations.

    However, in most cases, this is not the case, and filter parameters are used merely for filtering products, creating dozens of pages with duplicate content.

    Industry observers note that there may be multiple filter parameters in one URL. Identify which ones generate unwanted crawl space; do not block facets that form part of your search strategy. Google’s faceted-navigation guidance distinguishes these two cases.

    For example, if you have filters with the following parameters “sortby,” “color,” and “price,” you may use this set of rules:.

    According to recent reports, these pairs match each parameter in the first position or after another parameter. Add only the parameters you intend to restrict, and test both wanted and unwanted URLs.

    UTM parameters are used for tracking purposes.

    Industry observers note that in the Reddit exchange shown below, John Mueller addressed tracking parameters on external links. Keep that context separate from internally generated filter or search URLs.

    Keep internal links pointed at the URLs you want crawled. Decide whether to block a parameter by what it does on your site; the presence of a query string alone is not a reason to disallow a page.

    Let’s say you have a lot of PDF documents, such as product guides, brochures, or downloadable papers, and you don’t want them crawled.

    Here is a simple robots.txt rule that will block search engine bots from accessing those documents:.

    The “Disallow: /*.pdf$” line tells crawlers not to crawl any URLs that end with .pdf.

    By using /*, the rule matches any path on the website. As a result, any URL ending with .pdf will be blocked from crawling. It will not match /guide.pdf?download=1 or an uppercase .PDF extension; test any such variants separately. If you want a PDF excluded from search, use an X-Robots-Tag: noindex HTTP header and keep it crawlable so Google can read the header.

    If you have a WordPress website and want to disallow PDFs from the uploads directory where you upload them via the CMS, you can use the following rule:.

    You can see that we have conflicting rules here.

    In case of conflicting rules, the more specific one takes priority, which means the last line ensures that only the specific file located in folder “wp-content/uploads/2024/09/allowed-document.pdf” is allowed to be crawled.

    Let’s say you have an API endpoint where you submit your data from the form. It is likely your form has an action attribute like action=”/form/submissions/.”.

    Recent findings suggest that if a crawler discovers the URL /form/submissions/, you may want to prevent crawling of that path. You can request that with this rule:.

    By specifying a directory in the Disallow rule, you are telling the crawlers to avoid crawling all pages under that directory, and you don’t need to use the (*) wildcard anymore, like “/form/*.”.

    Note that you must always specify relative paths and never absolute URLs, like “https://www.example.com/form/” for Disallow and Allow directives.

    Sources indicate that be cautious to avoid malformed rules. For example, using /form without a trailing slash will also match a page /form-design-examples/, which may be a page on your blog that you want to index.

    Read: 8 Common Robots.txt Issues And How To Fix Them.

    If you have an ecommerce website, you likely have directories that start with “/myaccount/,” such as “/myaccount/orders/” or “/myaccount/profile/.”.

    With the top page “/myaccount/” being a sign-in page that you want to be indexed and found by people in search, you may want to disallow the subpages from being crawled by Googlebot.

    You can use the Disallow rule in combination with the Allow rule to block everything under the “/myaccount/” directory (except the /myaccount/ page).

    And again, since Google uses the most specific rule, it will disallow everything under the /myaccount/ directory but allow only the /myaccount/ page to be crawled.

    Here’s another use case of combining the Disallow and Allow rules: in case you have your search under the /search/ directory and want it to be found and indexed but block actual search URLs:.

    Every website uses JavaScript, and many of these scripts are not related to the rendering of content, such as tracking scripts or those used for loading AdSense.

    Only block a script after confirming it is unnecessary for rendering the content and links you want indexed. Use URL Inspection to check the rendered page; blocking a shared bundle or a script with rendering dependencies can prevent Google from seeing important content. A robots.txt file on your host also cannot control a script fetched from a different host.

    Below is a sample line that is disallowing sample JavaScript, which contains tracking pixels.

    You can block training bots while allowing AI tools to find your pages and retrieve them for people. The key is to give training, search, and user-requested AI crawlers separate rules.

    Industry observers note that publishers may block training to limit the use of their reporting without attribution, while ecommerce brands may welcome it if product mentions lead people to search and buy. Because the benefits differ by business, developers should set these rules with stakeholders.

    According to recent reports, disallowing training bots cannot guarantee that your content stays out of training datasets, because crawlers that ignore robots.txt can still collect it. It also does not force AI tools to visit or cite your site, as they may find the information elsewhere.

    According to recent reports, A BuzzStream study covered by SEJ in January 2026, found that 79% of the US and UK news sites examined disallowed at least one training bot, while 71% disallowed at least one retrieval or live-search bot. Because retrieval helps AI tools find and cite your pages, blocking those bots is a separate decision from opting out of training.

    Sources indicate that openAI uses OAI-SearchBot to surface websites in ChatGPT search answers, while ChatGPT-User handles user-requested visits. Because search and training permissions are separate, you can allow OAI-SearchBot and ChatGPT-User while blocking GPTBot.

    This example blocks OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s training crawlers while allowing their search and user-requested bots, along with Perplexity’s:.

    Industry observers note that in the example above, /private/ is an excluded directory. Replace it with any paths you want to keep those bots from crawling.

    Most major AI crawlers follow robots.txt, including OpenAI’s GPTBot and Anthropic’s ClaudeBot.

    User-requested visits work differently because some providers allow their bots to bypass robots.txt or generally ignore it when acting on a user’s request. OpenAI states robots.txt may not apply to ChatGPT-User, and Perplexity says Perplexity-User generally ignores it. Anthropic says its bots, including Claude-User, honor robots.txt. Because robots.txt only tells bots which URLs they may crawl, you need authentication to protect private content.

    The bot tokens and robots.txt policies for Copilot’s browser visits, Grok, DeepSeek, and Meta Muse remain unknown because I could not verify them in the providers’ public documentation.

    Google and Apple provide separate robots.txt tokens for controlling how crawled content is used:.

    Google-Extended covers Gemini training and specified grounding uses, where source content helps generate an answer. Blocking it does not block Googlebot or affect ordinary Google Search inclusion. Applebot-Extended controls foundation-model training without blocking Applebot’s search crawl. Neither token is a separate crawler, so these rules do not reduce crawling requests by themselves.

    After changing the file, check your server log files and confirm that your firewall allows the bots you want. Use server or CDN controls when you need to enforce access restrictions.

    For background, see SEJ’s earlier coverage of AI content use and AI chatbot traffic.

    Sources indicate that including your sitemap URL in the robots.txt file helps search engines easily discover all the important pages on your website. This is done by adding a specific line that points to your sitemap location, and you can specify multiple sitemaps, each on its own line.

    Unlike Allow or Disallow rules, which allow only a relative path, the Sitemap directive requires a full, absolute URL to indicate the location of the sitemap.

    Ensure the sitemaps’ URLs are accessible to search engines and have proper syntax to avoid errors.

    According to recent reports, the crawl-delay directive in robots.txt specifies the number of seconds a bot should wait before crawling the next page. While Googlebot does not recognize the crawl-delay directive, other bots may respect it.

    It helps prevent server overload by controlling how frequently bots crawl your site.

    For example, if you want ClaudeBot to crawl your content for AI training but want to avoid server overload, you can set a crawl delay to manage the interval between requests.

    This requests a 60-second delay from ClaudeBot, which Anthropic documents as supporting the non-standard Crawl-delay extension. Use this when you intend to allow that crawl. Adding a delay does not override a Disallow: / rule for the same bot; review the complete group rather than copying both policies.

    Of course, there may be AI bots that don’t respect crawl delay directives. In that case, you may need to use a web firewall to rate limit them.

    Once you’ve composed your robots.txt, you can use these tools to troubleshoot if the syntax is correct or if you didn’t accidentally block an crucial URL.

    Once you’ve updated your robots.txt, you must check whether it contains any error or accidentally blocks URLs you want to be crawled, such as resources, images, or website sections.

    Navigate to Settings > robots.txt to open the robots.txt report. It shows the files Google fetched and any parsing warnings or errors. You can request a recrawl after a critical change. To test whether an individual page is blocked, use URL Inspection.

    The video below illustrates the report workflow; interface details may differ from the current version.

    Google’s robots.txt parser is an open-source parser and matcher based on the implementation used in Google’s crawler.

    It requires advanced skills to install and run on your local computer. But it is highly recommended to take time and do it as instructed on that page because you can validate your changes in the robots.txt file before uploading to your server in line with the official Google parser.

    Robots.txt rules apply to the host, protocol, and port where the file is requested. If you need crawl restrictions on a subdomain, its robots.txt URL must serve the rules or redirect to a file that does; the parent domain’s file is not inherited.

    It creates challenges when you have a website with a dozen subdomains, as it means you should maintain a bunch of robots.txt files separately.

    However, it is possible to host a robots.txt file on a subdomain, such as https://cdn.example.com/robots.txt, and set up a redirect from https://www.example.com/robots.txt to it.

    You can do vice versa and host it only under the root domain and redirect from subdomains to the root.

    Google applies the retrieved rules to the host that originally requested robots.txt, not automatically to the host storing the shared file. Configure a redirect from each host you want to manage, and check that the shared paths make sense for all of them.

    It helps make updates and maintenance more efficient. Otherwise, you would need to use a separate robots.txt file for each subdomain.

    A properly optimized robots.txt file is crucial for managing a website’s crawl budget. It ensures that search engines like Googlebot spend their time on valuable pages rather than wasting resources on unnecessary ones.

    Blocking compliant crawlers can reduce unwanted requests. For AI systems, distinguish crawl restrictions from training-use controls, and verify the effect in your logs. Google-Extended and Applebot-Extended do not stop a separate crawler.

    Make sure you always validate your changes to avoid unexpected crawlability concerns.

    However, remember that crawl demand and serving capacity both matter. Useful content, efficient page loading, and a healthy server remain vital alongside robots.txt rules.
